ns2:section.sectionText: Description: This course surveys the history of the British Empire from the early modern period to the twentieth century. We will discuss the basic characteristics of British imperial power by examining encounters and struggles between Britons and colonized subjects across a range of locations in the Americas, the Pacific, South Asia, Africa, and Britain itself. In so doing, we will utilize a variety of printed and digital materials to explore what empire looked like for those people that are often missing from standard narratives of British imperial dominance, such as enslaved women and men, convicts, midwives, indigenous people, rebels, republicans, and other colonial subjects. In other words, this is a history of empire from below. The course will meet in person twice a week for lecture. There will also a weekly asynchronous remote assignment.
